text:
mira: FYI i'm kicking off a proposal to move small, frequently-read route attrs out of the big telemetry jsonb into a normalized console_route_attrs table. goal: reduce scan pressure for dashboard queries and improve p99s. looking for UX/rollout concerns
owen: +1. which attributes are you pulling? route_name, sla_tier, quota_window, active_flag?
mira: exactly. keep it narrow: route_name, owner_id, sla_tier, quota_bucket, disabled. everything else stays in jsonb. also index by (tenant_id, route_id).
sam: big question: how do we keep the console GraphQL resolvers consistent? front-end expects a single object. do we stitch in the API server or in SQL via a view?
priya: prefer SQL view for simplicity and fewer code paths. e.g. a read-only view that coalesces compact table with wide telemetry. fewer places to get wrong during rollout.
mira: thought: view approach means we can swap implementation under feature flag by changing view definition atomically. downside: view might be slower for some ad-hoc queries (joins).
owen: for high-throughput dashboard endpoints we should consider a read-adapter with simple in-memory merge for paging to avoid heavy db join on hot paths.
priya: we need telemetry to decide. add metrics: percent_reads_served_from_compact, avg_p99_compact_vs_wide, row_fetch_cost. alert if fallback > 3% for 15m.
sam: backfill plan options: (A) logical-copy per-tenant batches via COPY, (B) CDC stream to populate new table, (C) dualwrite from ingest and then backfill historical. pros/cons?
mira: preference C (dualwrite now, backfill historical). Reason: simplest rollback, can verify by checksum. Concern: dualwrite requires small change in ingest path + ff gating.
owen: also worry about index churn. If we create indexes on compact table upfront we'll bloat; create them partition-by-tenant and build per-partition after insert. Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY per-partition.
priya: can we leverage our existing partitioning by tenant_id? yes; make compact table partitioned by tenant_id. then backfill per-tenant into that partition and concurrently create indexes.
sam: estimate: current telemetry table ~900M rows; approx 850k routes across tenants, avg row 2.1KB. compact attrs ~120 bytes/row -> target dataset ~100MB per 100k routes. rough IO: copying 900M rows for just route-level attr subset will scan ~200GB compressed. at 60MB/s that's ~1 hour. but overhead, so pad to 3 hours with throttling.
mira: thanks for calc. we'll pick a low-traffic 8-hour window for each batch. infra: can we throttle to avoid impacting OLTP?
owen: yes, use pg_sleep between batches and set io limits. infra can monitor bgwriter and p99. i'll add a rate-limiter on the backfill job.
priya: migration safety: feature flag flow:
1) deploy compact table + migrations, no indexes yet
2) enable dualwrite behind FF for writes
3) start per-tenant backfill (partitioned) -> create indexes concurrently on that partition
4) enable read-optimized view for canary tenants via FF
5) if canary metrics stable -> ramp
6) after global success -> update view to drop jsonb columns or drop blobs

sam: rollback play: if we hit perf regressions, turn off read-FF and keep dualwrite for 7 days, then backfill remaining or revert dualwrite. ensure no destructive drop until 14 days.
mira: policy question: do we migrate data for tenants who have opted into long-term retention only? some enterprise tenants store route metadata for audit and we should honor opt-outs.
priya: add tenant-level allowlist. also add a flag to exclude regulated tenants from auto backfill and require manual approval.
owen: security/ACLs: compact table will be read by analytics and billing. create a sanitized view for billing with only the minimal columns and grant to billing_role. audit via event_log for any access.
sam: one more: dashboard pagination semantics. our current cursor encodes offset into single row fetch. moving attrs into another table means some queries that scanned jsonb->>fields will need new projections. we must ensure cursor integrity during canary.
mira: action: update GraphQL resolvers to call the view instead of raw table for list endpoints. implement a shallow smoke test that compares first/last 100 rows between view and old table for canary tenants.
priya: observability to add:
- compact_read_ratio (per-tenant)
- compaction_p99_delta (compacted p99 minus legacy p99)
- backfill_io_rate and backfill_progress
- fallback_rate alert (>3% for 15m)

ddl-bot: migration queued: 2026-04-compact-route-attrs v1. preview SQL generated.
owen: timeline proposal: staging run tomorrow evening, prod-canary next Wednesday (10 tenants), ramp over 10 business days.
mira: i'll assemble PR with migration + view + adapter stubs and link the canary list. please comment on schema types (text vs varchar vs smallint for sla_tier). prefer small schema to keep row size tiny.
sam: tiny nit: use enum for sla_tier to save space and avoid typos. also document default for missing attr -> coalesce rules in view.
priya: final note: add an entry in Console->Release notes explaining temporary UI fallbacks might occur during cutover. operations: schedule quiet window and a read-only degrade route if needed.
mira: great. action items:
- mira: PR + canary list + migration tasks
- owen: backfill rate-limiter + partition attach strategy doc
- sam: graphql/view smoke tests + cursor checks
- priya: observability cards + ACL views
- ddl-bot: run preview and schedule staging migration

ddl-bot: staging migration applied successfully. 3 warnings (concurrent index requires superuser).
mira: excellent. i'll post updates in #eng-platform-announce before staging run. thanks all :rocket:
